traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), : Pereskia grandifolia var. grandifolia: Shrubs or trees, erect, 2-10 m. Stems to 20 cm diam., very spiny; areoles to 12 mm diam. on basal portion of stem. Leaves elliptic-oblong, 6-30 × 3-9 cm, 0.5 mm thick. Spines all alike, 1-6 per areole, straight, acicular, 1-6.5 cm. Flowers 10-50 in dense cymose-paniculate aggregations, not fragrant, 1.5-3.2 × 3-7 cm; tepals epigynous; scales and areoles in distal 1/2 of receptacles; lateral pedicels 1-3 cm; terminal flower without pedicel; perianth pink. Fruits reddish green to yellowish green, pyriform or turbinate, often nearly as broad as long, 50-100 × 30-70 mm, often proliferating. Flowering not reported for Florida [year-round]. Spines all alike, so counted as radials with no centrals; their colour (not stated) a dark brown by hand.

traits.filament_colour.note: Britton and Rose, The Cactaceae vol. 1 (1919), p. 19, Pereskia grandifolia: 'sepals green; petals rose-colored, sometimes white; filaments red; style and stigma-lobes white'; FNA's genus: 'outer tepals often greenish, colored near margins'. The tepals' outer face a green by hand; the colours by hand from the words.

traits.young_areole_spines.note: Britton and Rose, The Cactaceae vol. 1 (1919), p. 19, Pereskia grandifolia: 'Tree or shrub, 2 to 5 meters high, usually with a definite, very spiny, woody trunk up to 1 dm. in diameter, the branches fleshy, glabrous, elongated, usually with 1 or 2 acicular spines at the areoles; leaves oblong, obtuse or acute, somewhat narrowed at base, 8 to 15 cm. long; petioles short; inflorescence terminal ... sepals green; petals rose-colored, sometimes white; filaments red; style and stigma-lobes white'. So a young branch's areoles carry 1 or 2 spines; the trunk's carry more (the FNA's up to 6).

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), : Pereskia grandifolia var. grandifolia: Shrubs or trees, erect, 2-10 m. Stems to 20 cm diam., very spiny; areoles to 12 mm diam. on basal portion of stem. Leaves elliptic-oblong, 6-30 × 3-9 cm, 0.5 mm thick. Spines all alike, 1-6 per areole, straight, acicular, 1-6.5 cm. Flowers 10-50 in dense cymose-paniculate aggregations, not fragrant, 1.5-3.2 × 3-7 cm; tepals epigynous; scales and areoles in distal 1/2 of receptacles; lateral pedicels 1-3 cm; terminal flower without pedicel; perianth pink. Fruits reddish green to yellowish green, pyriform or turbinate, often nearly as broad as long, 50-100 × 30-70 mm, often proliferating. Flowering not reported for Florida [year-round]. Pyriform written as obovoid and turbinate as obconic. 'Cymose-paniculate' drawn as a cyme, its flowers in dense branched clusters. The cluster's length is not stated: 10-50 flowers 3-7 cm across 'in dense ... aggregations' fill a rounded cluster about 10-25 cm long, by inference. Tepals epigynous, so the ovary inferior; flowering months left unstated: the flora gives only '[year-round]' where native, and a year-round season draws no gap between flowers and fruit; the colours by hand from 'pink' and 'reddish green to yellowish green'; typical height by hand toward the low end of 2-10 m.

Fruits reddish green to yellowish green, pyriform or turbinate, often nearly as broad as long, 50-100 × 30-70 mm, often proliferating. Flowering not reported for Florida [year-round]. Pyriform written as obovoid and turbinate as obconic. 'Cymose-paniculate' drawn as a cyme, its flowers in dense branched clusters. The cluster's length is not stated: 10-50 flowers 3-7 cm across 'in dense ... aggregations' fill a rounded cluster about 10-25 cm long, by inference. Tepals epigynous, so the ovary inferior; flowering months left unstated: the flora gives only '[year-round]' where native, and a year-round season draws no gap between flowers and fruit; the colours by hand from 'pink' and 'reddish green to yellowish green'; typical height by hand toward the low end of 2-10 m.
